top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P002) remains my first choice on voice, formal consequence and depth. On public knowledge, Autobiography of Red recasts the Geryon material as a verse novel, and Nox turns elegy into an act of translation, archive and the physical book. In both the learned apparatus is the route to grief and desire, not a display. The oeuvre spans lyric, verse novel, essay and drama over several decades and develops rather than repeats. I would rest the citation on the original writing (verse novel, elegy, essay-poems) and not name translation or classical scholarship as separate achievements. Cărtărescu (P001) is a close and serious second: his cumulative prose architecture meets a different standard of sustained significance, and I could support him anchored in the prose project, with poetry only as foundation. Tawada (P003) is third because her formal method is distributed across genres and two languages, a form of sustained achievement close to the one I credit in Carson. Reservations: Carson's most radical books depend on typography and design that translation cannot fully carry, her corpus is mostly short and hybrid, and I cannot show that the later work matches the best-known books. I have not read or independently verified any text, and this judgment rests on public knowledge only. Which standard of sustained significance weighs more, cumulative scale or formal renewal across genres, is a judgment I cannot settle from the evidence supplied. No award (P000) is last because I find the shortlist's leading candidates to meet the criteria on the stated reasoning.
